items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: We had a drum teacher there, Mr. McCullen, David McCullen, who was an ex army man from World War I that used to teach us all the different drum beats pieces.

ctx.x: ... they had a Drum and Bugle Corps, and every other Sunday, they would have a parade, and so at the age of 8, I joined this Drum and Bugle Corps. We had a drum teacher there, Mr. McCullen, David McCullen, who was an ex army man from World War I that used to teach us all the different drum beats pieces. And I would learn mine by ear, because I didn't know anything about reading any music, and I don't think he knew too much himself about reading music. But anyway, whatever the rhythms he would play on the marches…
were a nobody. I mean you had to have a band at your funeral; that meant that you were somebody.
